title: Tail Pathology Casebook: stage-contrib matrices and trace archetypes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working casebook of E2E trace archetypes observed during the Feb-March 2026 p50/p95/p99 survey. The goal is to capture representative trace shapes, per-stage contribution matrices, hypothesized root causes, and targeted next-step micro-experiments so we can move from ad-hoc debugging to reproducible mitigation playbooks.

Executive summary (short):
- p50 mostly dominated by model-forward + serialization; stable across seqlen.
- p95 driven by batching wait and kernel queue spikes for medium-length requests (seqlen 128-512).
- p99 dominated by two recurring archetypes: (A) cold KV-cache miss cascades + long disk read for large context blobs, and (B) tail batching stragglers caused by a small fraction of requests with large output widths or slow client RTTs.
- Actionable: (1) retire synchronous disk reads in hot-path (migrate to async cache warmers), (2) add per-request client-RTO annotation in traces, (3) stratified sampling to increase p99 capture rate for the two archetypes.

Instrumentation notes: what we have and what to add
- Existing spans: ingress-proxy, auth, deserialization, routing, kv-cache (hit/miss tag), batch-scheduler(wait_ms tag), gpu-queue, model-forward (model, seq_len, tokens_out), kv-cache-backfill (disk-read tag), serializer, egress.
- Missing / weak signals observed in tails: client RTT from edge, per-request memory pressure on worker, per-batch token-width distribution, kernel-retry/count of CUDA memcopies.
- Proposed additions: per-span cpu/alloc snapshots (lightweight), batch-level token-width histogram tag, 'client-rtt-ms' at ingress, and a boolean 'cold-kv-read' that marks disk fallback.

Sampling strategy we used for this doc
- Week-long rolling sample across three fleets: prod-hosted-us-west, dedicated-batch-1 (dc-eu-1), private-staging.
- 2% random sample for p50/p95 characterization; serpentine 100% capture for requests that hit kv-cache-backfill OR batch-scheduler wait > 25ms.
- Manual capture triggers: any trace with e2e > 1200ms and model-forward < 300ms (indicates non-model tail).

Trace archetypes (catalog):
1) Archetype: Model-Heavy (40% of traces overall; majority of p50)
   - Signature: ingress(10) -> batch-scheduler(6) -> gpu-queue(8) -> model-forward(250-400) -> serializer(20)
   - p50/p95/p99 footprint: model-forward dominates p50; p95 grows modestly with batch wait.
   - Hypothesis: Stable model runtime; variance from model-forward token count and small upcalls to decoder.
   - Mitigation: quantization variant A/B test, model kernel tune (mixed-precision), reduce serialization overhead with streaming.

2) Archetype: Batch-Queue Straggler (30% of p95, 60% of p99 cases)
   - Signature: ingress(8) -> batch-scheduler(wait large: 50-300) -> variable gpu-queue(1-150) -> model-forward(small) -> serializer
   - Observations: batch wait is often correlated with a small number of large-width requests or requests with client timeouts that cause delayed ACKs to the scheduler.
   - Tags commonly present: batch-size>32, batch-token-width-variance high, client-rtt-ms>100.
   - Hypotheses: conservative batching window + heterogeneous token widths; occasional client-side slow reads prevent batch closure.
   - Experiments: enforce max-batch-per-slot cap, introduce token-width-aware micro-batcher, and emit 'client-rtt-ms' to drive dynamic batching windows.

3) Archetype: Cold-KV Cascade (dominant in p99 for workloads with context fetches)
   - Signature: ingress -> routing -> kv-cache(miss) -> kv-cache-backfill(disk-read 120-800ms) -> batch-scheduler waits for backfill -> gpu-queue -> model-forward -> serializer
   - Per-stage breakdown example (p99 case): kv-cache-backfill 65%, batch-scheduler 10%, model-forward 12%, others 13%.
   - Root causes: large context blobs stored cold on blobstore, synchronous backfill and serialized disk I/O in same worker, poor prewarming heuristics.
   - Mitigations (priority): async backfill + early response streaming, prewarm heuristic tuned by request recency, move large-contexts to a fast tier (redis or local NVMe cache).

4) Archetype: Networking Edge Bounce (sporadic p99, cross-region)
   - Signature: ingress(proxy) shows long pre-ingress delay; egress shows similar pattern. client-rtt-ms tag > 200ms, often in cross-region flows or mobile clients.
   - Note: model-forward small; overall e2e inflated by external network.
   - Action: move routing policy to prefer local-region deployments for heavy flows; expose client-region hint to routing.

Quantitative p50/p95/p99 snapshots (example cohort: text-generation, seqlen 256, business-hours US-west):
- p50: 186ms
- p95: 382ms
- p99: 1,270ms
Breakdown (median contributions): ingress 8ms, deserial 5ms, routing 4ms, kv-cache 12ms, batch-scheduler 20ms, gpu-queue 18ms, model-forward 280ms, serializer 15ms, egress 10ms.
Note: the p99 breakdown skewed heavily to kv-cache-backfill or batch-scheduler depending on archetype.

Correlation and attribution heuristics used
- Per-trace normalized stage fraction: stage_ms / e2e_ms used to cluster traces into archetypes (k-means on normalized vectors).
- Gini coefficient over per-stage contributions used to identify single-stage dominated tails.
- Conditional histograms: p99 conditioned on seqlen bands (<128, 128-512, >512) to reveal seqlen-specific behaviors.

Key findings and recommended runbook items
1) Increase asynchronous cache warming for contexts referenced more than X times in 24h. (owner: Marcus, ETA: 2 sprints)
2) Instrument client-rtt-ms at ingress and surface in console per-route latency breakdowns. (owner: Sofia, ETA: 1 sprint)
3) Implement token-width-aware microbatcher prototype and run A/B on one fleet. (owner: Serving Runtime infra, ETA: 3 sprints)
4) Short-term mitigation: add a conservative max wait ceiling for batch-scheduler (e.g., 50ms) for routes with high batch-width variance. Monitor throughput impact. (owner: SRE + Serving Runtime)
5) For private deployments: add guidance to place context stores on NVMe tier or enable local-redis cache for high-context routes. (owner: Solutions Eng)

Open questions / unknowns
- How often are disk reads for backfill hitting cold storage vs mis-configured local eviction? Need sampling at storage layer.
- Does the presence of long-running client connections (mobile) correlate with specific customer SDK versions? (we should correlate user-agent tags)
- Are there model-specific kernel retries contributing to occasional long gpu-queue durations? Need low-level CUDA counters.

Planned micro-experiments (next 6 weeks)
- Week 1: enable client-rtt-ms and token-width histogram tags; increase p99 targeted capture to 10x for routes with >1% p99 error.
- Week 2-3: rollout async kv backfill on staging and run synthetic replay to validate no regression in correctness.
- Week 4: deploy microbatcher on canary fleet and compare p95/p99 delta against baseline.
- Week 5-6: collect results, refine prewarm heuristic, and draft release notes for Dedicated/Private config guidance.

Appendix: example trace snippet (flattened timings, ms)
- trace_id: tx-20260307-83f
- e2e: 1580
- ingress: 6
- deserial: 4
- routing: 3
- kv-cache: 2 (miss)
- kv-cache-backfill(disk-read): 980
- batch-scheduler: 120 (wait for backfill closure conflict)
- gpu-queue: 12
- model-forward: 320
- serializer: 25
- egress: 8

Notes for doc readers:
- This is intentionally a practical playbook not a rigorous academic writeup. The archetype percentages are approximate and sampled from broad production slices — treat as directional.
- If you add traces, append to the archetype catalogue and include a minimal »why I think this is similar« note.

Immediate action log (short):
- 2026-02-12: Started targeted p99 capture for kv backfill.
- 2026-02-20: Prototype token-width hist tagging merged to feature branch.
- 2026-03-02: First canary run with async backfill on staging; no functional regressions, p99 dropped ~18% on staging for context-heavy routes.

Owner notes:
- Ava: prioritizing instrumentation to reduce blind spots; will coordinate with Observability for retention and indexing (avoid 100% trace retention costs).
- Marcus: taking lead on async backfill prototype and storage tiering guidance.

If you see a new tail not captured here, add it under ARCHETYPE X with an example trace and one-line hypothesis.

----
End of casebook entry.
